title: Canary Islands Cruises: Winter Sun at Sea
description: Compare Canary Islands cruise deals: Tenerife, Gran Canaria, Lanzarote and Madeira. No-fly cruises from Southampton and fly-cruises.
cardText: Winter sunshine in Tenerife, Gran Canaria and Lanzarote, often with Madeira, by fly-cruise or straight from the UK.
intro: Mild winters, volcanic landscapes and black-sand beaches. Compare Canary Islands cruise deals, from no-fly sailings out of the UK to fly-cruises based in the islands.

image.alt: Golden beach and harbour below green mountains on the coast of Tenerife

sections.html:
• Tenerife (Santa Cruz): the gateway to Mount Teide National Park.
  • Gran Canaria (Las Palmas): a lively city with a long urban beach.
  • Lanzarote (Arrecife): volcanic scenery, including Timanfaya National Park.
  • La Palma and Fuerteventura: quieter islands on some itineraries.
  • Madeira (Funchal, Portugal): often paired with the Canaries, known for its gardens and its New Year’s Eve fireworks.
  • Longer itineraries may also call at Lisbon, Cádiz (for Seville) or ports in Morocco.

sections.h2: When to cruise the Canary Islands
sections.html: The Canary Islands have a mild climate all year, which makes them one of the most popular winter-sun cruise regions for UK and European travellers, roughly from autumn to spring. Many ships move to the Canaries for the northern winter, when the Mediterranean is cooler and quieter.

From the UK: round trips from Southampton and other UK ports usually take around two weeks, including several sea days crossing the Bay of Biscay, which can be rough in winter.

Fly-cruise: some ships sail round trips from Tenerife or Gran Canaria in winter, so you can fly out and spend almost every day in port. US travellers usually combine a Canaries cruise with a European trip or a transatlantic crossing.

sections.h2: Tips for a Canary Islands cruise
sections.html:
• Pack layers: it’s warm by day, but evenings at sea and the Bay of Biscay can be cool.
  • Book popular trips such as Mount Teide early, as they can sell out.
  • The Canary Islands are part of Spain and the Schengen area, so check current entry rules.

faqs.q: What is the best month for a Canary Islands cruise?
faqs.a: The islands are mild all year. Cruises are most popular from autumn to spring, when they offer winter sun compared with northern Europe.

faqs.q: How long is a Canary Islands cruise from Southampton?
faqs.a: Many are around 12 to 14 nights, including several days at sea each way.

faqs.q: Is the Bay of Biscay rough?
faqs.a: It can be, especially in winter. Modern ships have stabilisers, but if you’re prone to seasickness, pack a remedy and choose a mid-ship cabin on a lower deck, or consider a fly-cruise.

blocks.title: Ways to save on Canary Islands cruises
blocks.intro: Real cruise offers take a few common forms. Here’s how each works and where to look.

items.title: No-fly cruises
items.text: Sail from Southampton and other UK ports: no airport queues and more generous luggage.

items.title: Fly-cruise packages
items.text: Flights, transfers and cruise booked together, often with extra protection such as ATOL in the UK.

items.title: Last-minute cruises
items.text: Unsold cabins close to sailing can be discounted. Best if you can travel at short notice.

items.title: Repositioning cruises
items.text: One-way voyages as ships move between regions, often with many sea days and good value per night.
